item: Gizmodo report on SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories)
finding: Gizmodo reported on the FAA's SMART system, an $875 million effort drawing on about 200 data feeds. The report itself is real. The Nov. 10 Gizmodo article is still online and describes that expansion and those figures, citing the FAA and Ars Technica. This confirms that the report exists, not that SMART caused today's outage. [Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347)
label: C

finding: No evidence links SMART to the failure. It was expanded to all 22 en route centers three days earlier. Mullin said on the record that CISA is "looking at that" ([GeekWire](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/dhs-chief-sees-no-microsoft-link-to-faa-ground-stop-says-possible-ai-role-being-investigated/)); that he said this is confirmed, but any actual SMART role is unconfirmed. Vendor Air Space Intelligence posted on X that the ground stop "is not based on or a result of the SMART system" (quoted by GeekWire). SMART only advises, and FAA specialists review every recommendation. AvWeb quotes Duffy saying SMART is not connected to STARS or ERAM and that "There's no possible way SMART would have impacted what happened." AeroTime also reports he ruled SMART out. A SMART role stays unconfirmed because Reuters has Mullin saying a rogue AI is not fully ruled out. [AvWeb](https://avweb.com/aviation-news/faa-nationwide-ground-stop-lifts-smart-ai/)
label: R

finding: A non-story. The Bloomberg quote was most likely a subscriber alert or social post echoing FAA Command Center wording about ATC frequency impacts, not new reporting.
label: D

item: D.C. National reporting multiple frequency outages
finding: Reagan National was held under the national stop, which is confirmed. That is consistent with the Potomac Approach SWANN/AGARD stops at 3:31 PM and the Washington Center frequency stops at 3:33 and 3:41 PM, per IFR Meter. A 4:14 PM Reagan National arrivals stop for "gridlock" is IFR Meter only and was not found in numbered advisories. A unique tower failure, and the specific frequencies named in an r/aviation post, remain unconfirmed. [ARLnow](https://www.arlnow.com/2026/11/13/developing-flights-halted-at-reagan-national-and-dulles-amid-nationwide-faa-ground-stop/) · [IFR Meter](https://ifrmeter.com/blog/national-ground-stop-2026-11-13)
label: R

item: Former DOT Inspector General Mary Schiavo on SMART timing
finding: On CNN Friday afternoon she called the SMART timing "just too much of a coincidence," while saying she did not know if they were linked. She described the SMART expansion as starting "today" (Friday); that timing is incorrect. The FAA expanded SMART to all 22 en route centers on Tuesday, Nov. 10, three days before the outage. NPR interviewed her on Weekend Edition Saturday at 7:40 AM ET, but the page said audio would be available later and no transcript has been posted, so no new Saturday quotes are confirmed. This is commentary, not an official finding. [Mediaite](https://www.mediaite.com/media/news/cnn-aviation-analyst-says-its-just-too-much-of-a-coincidence-faa-rolled-out-new-ai-traffic-tool-right-before-nationwide-comms-outage/) · [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/14/nx-s1-6040518/former-dot-inspector-general-mary-schiavo-on-fridays-faa-ground-stop)
